cases.issue_title: [BUG] Mail rule loops forever when all attachments are duplicates (no ProcessedMail row created)
cases.issue_body:
### Description

If **every** attachment of a mail is rejected as a duplicate, the mail is never
recorded in `ProcessedMail`. As a result the mail rule picks it up again on every
single mail fetch, for as long as it stays inside the rule's `maximum_age` window.

On our instance two such mails produced **~11,900 failed consume tasks** over four
weeks — one of them 2,645 attempts per attachment, at one attempt every 10 minutes.
No data is lost, but the task list becomes unusable: genuine failures drown in the
noise (30,940 task rows, 18,181 of them duplicate rejections).

### Root cause

`queue_consumption_tasks()` in `src/paperless_mail/mail.py` wires the consume tasks
as a chord header and `apply_mail_action` as the body, with `error_callback` attached
via `.on_error()`:

```python
chord(header=consume_tasks, body=mail_action_task).on_error(
    error_callback.s(...)
).delay()
```

* `apply_mail_action` (writes `ProcessedMail`, applies the rule action) only runs if
  **all** header tasks succeed.
* `error_callback` is supposed to write `ProcessedMail(status="FAILED")` in the
  failure case — and normally does, so the mechanism works for mails where only
  *some* attachments fail.
* But Celery's default `task_allow_error_cb_on_chord_header=False` means the errback
  is **not** invoked for failing *header* tasks. Celery logs this on every run:

```
CPendingDeprecationWarning: task_allow_error_cb_on_chord_header=False is pending
deprecation in a future release of Celery. Please test the new behavior by setting
task_allow_error_cb_on_chord_header to True ...

[ERROR] [django_celery_results.backends.database] Chord '<id>' raised:
ConsumerError('<file>.pdf: Not consuming <file>.pdf: It is a duplicate of <doc> (#<id>).')
```

No errback → no `ProcessedMail` row → the skip check in `_handle_mail_rule()`
(`ProcessedMail.objects.filter(rule=..., uid=..., folder=...).exists()`) never
matches → the mail is fetched again on the next run.

We verified this against the database: for the two looping mails there is **no**
`ProcessedMail` row at all, while the same rule holds 181 `FAILED` rows for other
mails (those had at least one attachment that consumed successfully).

### Why it is easy to hit

Any correspondence that repeatedly ships the same enclosures triggers it: the first
mail imports them, every later mail in the thread carries only known files. In
document-heavy workflows this is routine rather than exceptional — the same set of
enclosures travels with every letter in a thread.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a mail rule consuming PDF attachments, action "tag mail".
2. Send a mail with attachment A, let it be consumed.
3. Send a second mail whose **only** attachment is the identical file A.
4. The second mail is fetched again on every scheduled run; no IMAP tag is set and
   no `ProcessedMail` row appears.

### Suggested fix

Set `CELERY_TASK_ALLOW_ERROR_CB_ON_CHORD_HEADER = True` in `src/paperless/settings.py`.
Celery's own warning recommends the new behaviour and it is pending deprecation.

An alternative that does not depend on Celery semantics: create the `ProcessedMail`
row when the tasks are queued and update its status afterwards, so a mail can never
be picked up twice regardless of task outcome.

Related: #3919 — the same deprecation warning was reported in 2023 and closed as
"just a warning". The consequence for the error path appears to have gone unnoticed.

### Versions

* paperless-ngx 2.20.14 (setting is still absent in 3.1.2)
* celery 5.5.3
* PostgreSQL, Docker, `django-celery-results` database backend

*(Log excerpts anonymised — document titles and mail subjects contained client data.)*

cases.issue_title: Apply AI suggestions workflow action never runs on DOCUMENT_ADDED: task queued inside the consumer's transaction
cases.issue_body:
### Description

The `APPLY_AI_SUGGESTIONS` workflow action never runs when the workflow trigger is `DOCUMENT_ADDED`, because the Celery task is queued from inside the consumer's `transaction.atomic()` block and picked up before that transaction commits. The worker's own DB connection cannot see the document, `Document.objects.get()` raises `DoesNotExist`, and the handler logs a warning and returns.

The relevant code, on 3.1.2:

- `documents/consumer.py:597` opens `with transaction.atomic():`
- `documents/consumer.py:673` sends `document_consumption_finished` **inside** that block
- that signal runs `run_workflows_added` -> `run_workflows(trigger_type=DOCUMENT_ADDED, ...)`
- `documents/signals/handlers.py:1006` queues the action with `apply_ai_suggestions.delay(action_id=..., document_id=...)`
- `documents/tasks.py:735-743` then fails the lookup and logs:

```
Workflow action %s or document %s no longer exists, not applying AI suggestions
```

Two things make this hard to notice:

1. **The log message points at the wrong object.** It names the action first, so it reads as if the workflow action were missing. The action exists; the document is simply not visible yet.
2. **If the workflow also has an `ASSIGNMENT` action that adds a marker tag, that action runs synchronously and succeeds.** So the document ends up tagged as though AI had been applied while no suggestion was ever fetched. In our case that masked the failure for five days across every consumed document.

The reliable tell is the task duration: the task "succeeded" in ~0.04s, where a real suggestion call against our LLM backend takes ~5.5s.

`DOCUMENT_UPDATED` triggers are not affected, because `ATOMIC_REQUESTS` is `False` and an API request commits before the signal fires. That also means a workflow tested on `DOCUMENT_UPDATED` will appear to work and then fail in production on `DOCUMENT_ADDED`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an LLM backend and confirm `/api/documents/<id>/ai_suggestions/` returns suggestions.
2. Create a workflow with trigger type **Document Added** and a single **Apply AI suggestions** action, with some fields selected.
3. Consume a document (any source).
4. Observe the warning in the webserver log, no metadata applied, and the task recorded as succeeded in a few tens of milliseconds.

Repeating steps 2-4 with the trigger changed to **Document Updated** and driving it with an API `PATCH` works as expected, which isolates the transaction as the cause rather than the action.

### Suggested fix

Queue the task after the surrounding transaction commits, e.g. in `documents/signals/handlers.py`:

```python
from django.db import transaction

transaction.on_commit(
    lambda: apply_ai_suggestions.delay(
        action_id=action.pk,
        document_id=document.pk,
    ),
)
```

`on_commit` runs the callback immediately when there is no active atomic block, so this is safe for the `DOCUMENT_UPDATED` path too.

It may also be worth reordering the warning in `documents/tasks.py` to distinguish a missing action from a missing document, since those two cases have very different causes.

### Webserver logs

```
[WARNING] [paperless.tasks] Workflow action 60 or document 3658 no longer exists, not applying AI suggestions
```

Surrounding context showed `document_consumption_finished` dispatched, the task received ~180ms later, and the task completing successfully in 0.0399s with no LLM request made.

### Paperless-ngx version

3.1.2

### Host OS

x86_64 Linux (Unraid 7.3.2)

### Installation method

Docker - official image

### Configuration changes

AI enabled via environment variables with an OpenAI-compatible backend. No relevant overrides in the database.

cases.issue_title: [BUG] Download filename of a versioned document uses the version's own metadata, not the document shown in the UI
cases.issue_body:
### Description

When a document has more than one version, the filename offered on download is built from the **version's own metadata**, which silently diverges from the metadata of the root document shown in the UI. The result is that a document that is correctly titled in the web interface downloads under a stale name — typically the raw scanner filename — together with a correspondent and a date the user never assigned.

There are two separate causes that combine:

**1. The version's metadata is overwritten right after being copied.**

`ConsumerPlugin._create_version_from_root()` (`src/documents/consumer.py`) deliberately copies `title` and `created` from the root document into the new version:

```python
version_doc = Document(
    root_document=root_doc_frozen,
    version_index=next_version_index + 1,
    ...
    created=root_doc_frozen.created,
    title=root_doc_frozen.title,
    ...
)
```

But immediately afterwards, `document_consumption_finished` is dispatched with the **version** as `document` (`consumer.py`, in the `if self.input_doc.root_document_id:` branch):

```python
document = Document.objects.prefetch_related("versions").get(pk=document.pk)

document_consumption_finished.send(
    sender=self.__class__,
    document=document,
    logging_group=self.logging_group,
    classifier=classifier,
    ...
)
```

The matching/classification handlers then run against the version and overwrite `created`, and assign `correspondent`, `document_type`, `storage_path` and `tags` (including the inbox tag) from the file's own text. So the intent expressed by `_create_version_from_root` is undone one step later.

Observed on a real install, the dates parsed for versions were taken from unrelated numbers in the OCR text — one version ended up with a `created` date in the 1940s, while its root document is correctly dated 2026. Correspondents assigned to versions were, in most cases, not the correspondent of the root document.

**2. Later edits to the root document are never propagated to its versions.**

Once the user corrects title/correspondent/date on the document in the UI, the version keeps the values it was given at consumption time. Nothing reconciles them.

**Why this surfaces on download:** `file_response()` resolves the *effective* (latest) version and passes it to `serve_file()`, which builds `Content-Disposition` from `doc.get_public_filename()` — i.e. `Document.__str__` → `"{created} {correspondent} {title}"` **of the version**:

```python
filename = doc.filename if follow_formatting else doc.get_public_filename()
```

So the UI renders the root document's metadata while the download is named after the version's. On an install with 1895 documents, all 12 documents that had a second version were affected; documents without versions are fine, which makes the behaviour look random to users.

Note that `Document.filename` (the on-disk path) of the version *is* derived from the root and stays correct — only the public/download name is wrong. That inconsistency is a good indication of which of the two is unintended.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Consume a scanned PDF, e.g. `20260801_130559.pdf`. Paperless sets `title = "20260801_130559"`.
2. Open the document and use the built-in PDF editor (e.g. rotate a page), then save. A new version is created from `<id>_edited.pdf`.
3. Now give the document a proper title, correspondent, document type and date in the UI.
4. Download the document.

Expected: the download is named after the metadata shown in the UI, e.g. `2026-06-17 Correspondent A Some proper title.pdf`.

Actual: the download is named after the version's metadata, e.g. `2026-01-01 Correspondent B 20260801_130559.pdf` — raw scanner name, a correspondent the user never picked, and a date parsed from the document text.

The divergence can be listed directly:

```python
for v in Document.objects.filter(root_document__isnull=False):
    r = v.root_document
    print(r.pk, v.pk, r.title, "<>", v.title, "|", r.correspondent, "<>", v.correspondent)
```

### Webserver logs

cases.issue_title: bulk_edit modify_custom_fields stores values that CustomFieldInstanceSerializer rejects
cases.issue_body:
> **Correction (see comment below):** the original version of this report claimed that *any* `PATCH` on the affected document fails. That was wrong — I inferred it instead of testing it. Only requests that **send the custom fields back** fail. The body below is corrected and restructured to follow the bug report template, which I should not have bypassed. Sorry for the noise.

### Description

`POST /api/documents/bulk_edit/` with `method: modify_custom_fields` stores custom field values **without validating them**, while `CustomFieldInstanceSerializer` does validate. A value longer than `max_length` can therefore be written through one API endpoint and is afterwards rejected by the other — so any client that reads a document and writes it back (round-tripping `custom_fields`, which is the normal REST pattern) gets a `400` it cannot fix without first discovering and shortening the stored value.

`documents/bulk_edit.py::modify_custom_fields` writes straight through the ORM:

```python
CustomFieldInstance.objects.update_or_create(
    document_id=doc_id,
    field_id=field_id,
    defaults=defaults,
)
```

`Model.save()` does not run validators, and `CustomFieldInstance.value_text` is a `CharField(max_length=128)` — a validator, not a database constraint. On SQLite (`VARCHAR` length is not enforced by the engine) the oversized value is stored silently.

What makes this expensive in practice is the delay and the misattribution: the write succeeds, and the failure surfaces later, in a different component, on a request that has nothing to do with the field. In our instance 182 of 384 documents carried such a value before we noticed.

### Steps to reproduce

Measured on 3.0.4, SQLite, against a throwaway custom field:

1. Create a custom field of type `string`.
2. Write a 200-character value through bulk_edit:

```bash
curl -X POST "$PAPERLESS/api/documents/bulk_edit/" \
  -H "Authorization: Token $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"documents":[<DOC>],"method":"modify_custom_fields",
       "parameters":{"add_custom_fields":{"<FIELD>":"xxx…200 chars…xxx"},
                     "remove_custom_fields":[]}}'
```

   → **`200 OK`**. `GET /api/documents/<DOC>/` returns all 200 characters.

3. `PATCH /api/documents/<DOC>/` **without** `custom_fields` (e.g. `{"archive_serial_number": null}`)
   → **`200 OK`**. *(This is the part I got wrong originally — an isolated PATCH is unaffected.)*

4. `PATCH /api/documents/<DOC>/` **with** the document's `custom_fields` sent back unchanged
   → **`400 Bad Request`**.

5. Same request after replacing the value with a short one
   → **`200 OK`**.

So step 2 and step 4 disagree about what is a valid value.

### Webserver logs

The rejection is an API response rather than a server-side traceback; this is the body returned in step 4:

```json
{"custom_fields": [{}, {"value": ["Ensure this value has at most 128 characters (it has 200)."]}]}
```

### Paperless-ngx version

3.0.4

### Host OS

Debian aarch64 (Rockchip RK3588 SBC)

### Installation method

Docker - official image

### System status

Django 5.2.16, Python 3.12.13, SQLite.

### Browser logs

n/a — reproduced entirely through the REST API.

### Other

Field types without a length limit exist (`longtext` → `value_long_text`, a `TextField`), so this concerns `string` and `monetary` (`max_length=128`) and `select` (`max_length=16`).

On PostgreSQL a `varchar(128)` column would presumably raise at the database layer instead of storing silently — a different symptom, but the same gap: `bulk_edit` does no validation of its own.

Happy to test a patch, and happy to close this and re-file through the form if you prefer.

cases.issue_title: Actions: one invalid scheduled workflow prevents all other scheduled workflows from starting
cases.issue_body:
### Description

A validation error in one scheduled workflow aborts the entire **Start actions schedule tasks** cron pass, so unrelated scheduled workflows are not enqueued.

This was observed on Gitea 1.27.2. One scheduled workflow called a reusable workflow and passed a secret that the called workflow did not declare. The validation error is correct, but the scheduler stops processing after that entry instead of recording the failure for that workflow and continuing with the remaining due schedules.

### Reproduction

1. Create two repositories with scheduled workflows.
2. In the first repository, create a workflow with a due `schedule:` that calls a reusable workflow and passes a secret not declared under `on.workflow_call.secrets` in the called workflow:

```yaml
jobs:
  test:
    uses: https://gitea.example/shared/workflows/.gitea/workflows/reusable.yml@main
    secrets:
      TEST_SECRET: ${{ secrets.TEST_SECRET }}
```

3. In the second repository, create an otherwise valid workflow with a due `schedule:`.
4. Wait for the scheduler cron task.

### Actual behaviour

The cron task fails every minute with an error similar to:

```
CreateScheduleTask: InsertRun: inline trigger caller <id> ready:
caller "test" secrets: caller secret "TEST_SECRET" is not declared
in the called workflow's on.workflow_call.secrets
```

No later scheduled workflows are enqueued. Manual `workflow_dispatch` runs still work.

After removing/commenting the invalid secret mapping, the next scheduler pass succeeds and unrelated scheduled workflows resume immediately.

### Expected behaviour

The invalid workflow should be rejected and logged (or represented as a failed run), but the scheduler should continue processing other due schedules in the same pass.

### Environment

- Gitea 1.27.2
- Official `gitea/gitea:1.27-rootless` Docker image
- PostgreSQL
- Gitea Actions runner 2.3.0

### Related issues

- #39064 documents the reusable-workflow secret validation, which is expected behaviour.
- #36967 shows the same scheduler-wide failure mode for a panic during scheduled-workflow parsing. This report is specifically about ordinary validation errors aborting the scheduler loop.

cases.issue_title: Actions: step-level `continue-on-error` rejects expressions and fails the whole workflow file
cases.issue_body:
**Gitea Version**

```
1.27.0-dev
```

**What happened?**

On GitHub Actions, `jobs.<job_id>.steps[*].continue-on-error` accepts an expression and
the `steps` context is available there. In Gitea the same workflow does not just ignore
the expression — it fails to parse, and the failure takes down the entire workflow file,
not only that step.

Reproducer:

    name: test
    on: push
    jobs:
      job1:
        runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
        steps:
          - id: quarantine
            run: echo "quarantine=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          - run: exit 1
            continue-on-error: ${{ steps.quarantine.outputs.quarantine == 'true' }}

Result:

    invalid jobs: yaml: unmarshal errors:
      line 10: cannot unmarshal !!str `${{ ste...` into bool

Expected: the expression is passed through and evaluated by the runner at step execution
time, as it is on GitHub Actions.

Cause: `modules/actions/jobparser/model.go:185` types the field as a plain bool, so any
non-boolean scalar aborts job decoding:

    ContinueOnError  bool  `yaml:"continue-on-error,omitempty"`

The runner side already handles this correctly — `act/model/workflow.go:650` keeps it as
`RawContinueOnError string` and `act/runner/step.go:280` evaluates it against a
step-scoped expression evaluator (`NewStepExpressionEvaluator`,
`DefaultStatusCheckNone`). So the capability exists in the runner and is only blocked by
the server-side parser.

The server itself never reads the step field — grepping for reads of
`Step.ContinueOnError` outside tests finds none; it only needs to survive the
SingleWorkflow round-trip into the job payload. Changing it to `RawContinueOnError string`
(or a `yaml.Node`, mirroring how the job-level field is handled) should be enough to let
it through untouched.

Note that the job-level `continue-on-error` added in #38100 does not cover this use case:
that expression is evaluated once when the run is created and frozen into the
`continue_on_error` column (`services/actions/run.go:217`), so only `github`, `matrix`,
`strategy`, `vars` and `inputs` are in scope — `steps` is unavailable and
`needs.*.outputs` is still empty at that point. Any decision that is only known once a
step has run therefore has no supported expression form today.

cases.issue_title: A deleted Actions run is retried forever in the actions_ready_job queue
cases.issue_body:
### Gitea Version

1.27.2, and 1.27.1 before it. `services/actions/job_emitter.go` is unchanged on main @ 475e51c7.

### What happened?

If a repository is deleted while one of its Actions runs still has a pending job update in `actions_ready_job`, that queue item can never be handled, and it is retried forever.

`services/actions/job_emitter.go` on main:

```go
if err := checkJobsByRunID(ctx, update.RunID); err != nil {
    log.Error("check run %d: %v", update.RunID, err)
    ret = append(ret, update)      // returned as unhandled, so the queue re-pushes it
}

func checkJobsByRunID(ctx context.Context, runID int64) error {
    run, exist, err := db.GetByID[actions_model.ActionRun](ctx, runID)
    if !exist {
        return fmt.Errorf("run %d does not exist", runID)   // never becomes true again
    }
```

The run is gone, so the error is permanent, but it is reported as unhandled and pushed back. There is no retry bound and no dead letter, so the only way out is to stop Gitea and delete the queue store.

This has happened four times on our instance. The two I still have logs for:

- run 12144, 08-09 to 08-10: 89,450 log lines, 9.3% of everything Gitea logged in those days.
- run 16919, from 08-19 05:44:03 until we deleted the store the next day: about 49,000 lines in 22 hours, one every 1.6 seconds.

For 16919 the cause is in the same second:

```text
05:44:03 router: completed DELETE /api/v1/repos/<owner>/<scratch-repo> ... 204 No Content
05:44:03 jobEmitterQueueHandler [E] check run 16919: run 16919 does not exist
```

It also crowds out the rest of the log, which is its own problem when you are trying to investigate something else.

To reproduce: delete a repository while one of its runs still has jobs that have not settled.

A deleted run has nothing to emit, so I think the item should be treated as handled rather than returned. Happy to send a PR if you would like one.

Related, but not the same problem: https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/issues/33882

### How are you running Gitea?

Docker `gitea/gitea:1.27.2` on Docker Swarm, PostgreSQL 16.

<sub>Written by Claude Code (Opus 5).</sub>

cases.issue_title: Organizations with limited visibility hide every tab except Repositories for non-members
cases.issue_body:
### Gitea Version
1.27.0

### What happened?
An organization set to Limited ("Visible only to authenticated users") shows a signed-in non-member only the Repositories tab. Packages, Code and Projects are gone from the org menu. Packages still loads if the URL is entered directly, despite the hidden tab; Code and Projects return 404. The same organization set to Public shows all of these tabs to everyone, including anonymous visitors.

Expected behaviour: `limited` should show the same tabs as `public`, with the audience narrowed to authenticated users.

***Root cause***

`Organization.UnitPermission()` in `models/organization/org.go`:

```go
if doer != nil {
	teams, _ := GetUserOrgTeams(ctx, org.ID, doer.ID)
	if len(teams) > 0 {
		return teams.UnitMaxAccess(unitType)
	}
}

if org.Visibility.IsPublic() {
	return perm.AccessModeRead
}
return perm.AccessModeNone
```

A signed-in non-member has no teams in the org, so it skips the first block. `IsPublic()` is a strict `== VisibleTypePublic`, so `limited` falls through to `AccessModeNone`.

That one check causes both symptoms:

**Hidden tabs** — `services/context/org.go`:

```go
ctx.Data["CanReadProjects"] = ctx.Org.CanReadUnit(ctx, unit.TypeProjects)
ctx.Data["CanReadPackages"] = ctx.Org.CanReadUnit(ctx, unit.TypePackages)
ctx.Data["CanReadCode"]     = ctx.Org.CanReadUnit(ctx, unit.TypeCode)
```

`CanReadUnit()` just wraps `UnitPermission()`, and `templates/org/menu.tmpl` shows the tabs only `{{if .CanReadPackages}}` etc. All three are false, so all three tabs vanish. Repositories stays because it uses repo-level visibility, not this function.

**404s** — `reqUnitAccess` in `routers/web/web.go`, used on `/-/code` and `/-/projects`:

```go
if ctx.Org.Organization.UnitPermission(ctx, ctx.Doer, unitType) < accessMode {
	ctx.NotFound(nil)
}
```

**Packages still loads**, because that route uses a different guard, `determineAccessMode()` in `services/context/package.go`, which handles `limited` correctly:

```go
if accessMode == perm.AccessModeNone && organization.HasOrgOrUserVisible(ctx, pkgOwner, doer) {
	accessMode = perm.AccessModeRead
}
```

So the page is served, but the tab linking to it is hidden. `UnitPermission()` is the only place that checks `IsPublic()` instead of `HasOrgOrUserVisible()`.

### How are you running Gitea?
Official `gitea/gitea` Docker image running on Kubernetes managed by Rancher, with PostgreSQL as the database.

### Description of the bug

I tried to upgrade my server from 10.11.11 to the latest unstable build (2026072708) and it won't start. The startup migrations run for 30-40 seconds, then one called `20260724185102_AddPrimaryVersionIdIndex` fails with `SQLite Error 19: 'UNIQUE constraint failed: Users.NormalizedUsername'`. The database gets rolled back and the health check reports Unhealthy forever. Same error on every restart, I tried 3 times.

Since the error mentions usernames, I figured maybe I had two users with the same name. So I stopped the server and opened jellyfin.db with sqlite3. I have 10 users and there are no duplicates, not even when comparing case-insensitively:

```sql
SELECT NormalizedUsername, COUNT(*) FROM Users GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
SELECT UPPER(Username), COUNT(*) FROM Users GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
```

Both come back empty.

One thing I noticed: `.schema Users` shows the index it's trying to create (`IX_Users_NormalizedUsername`) is already in the database. I don't know if that's normal or part of the problem.

The rollback works at least. After each failed start the db file is back to how it was, and 10.11.11 boots fine again when I switch back to it.

Before posting this I read through a bunch of issues here and the RC release notes to check if I had missed any upgrade instructions I was supposed to follow. I was already on 10.11.11 so I think I met the requirements. I also tried troubleshooting with Claude, which is where the sqlite3 poking around came from. Nothing worked.

### Reproduction steps

1. Have a working 10.11.11 server with some users (I have 10). I'm using the linuxserver.io docker image.
2. Stop the container.
3. Switch the image to the unstable build (`lscr.io/linuxserver/jellyfin:nightly-2026072708ubu2604-ls92`, Jellyfin 12.0.0).
4. Start it and watch the logs.
5. Migrations run for a bit, then it dies on `20260724185102_AddPrimaryVersionIdIndex` with the UNIQUE constraint error and startup never finishes. Happens every time for me.

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

Startup fails during the database migrations with `SQLite Error 19: 'UNIQUE constraint failed: Users.NormalizedUsername'`. The database gets rolled back and the server never finishes starting. This happens even though my Users table has no duplicate usernames.

The migrations finish and the server starts.

cases.issue_title: [Bug] [Master] Recovering a failed workflow changes a forced-success task to SUCCESS
cases.issue_body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the existing issues and found no issue reporting the same status transition.

### What happened

After a failed task instance is manually set to forced success, its state is correctly changed to `FORCED_SUCCESS`.

If the workflow instance is then recovered using "Recovery Failed":

- the forced-success task is skipped as expected;
- downstream tasks continue to run;
- but the state of the forced-success task instance is changed from `FORCED_SUCCESS` to `SUCCESS`.

The workflow can continue normally, but the information indicating that the task was completed through manual intervention is lost. The task then appears to have completed successfully through normal execution.

This behavior was reproduced on a deployment based on 3.4.2 and was also confirmed in the current `dev` branch source code.

### What you expected to happen

After recovering the failed workflow:

- the forced-success task should be treated as successful for dependency and workflow topology evaluation;
- downstream tasks should continue to run;
- the task instance state should remain `FORCED_SUCCESS`.

Recovering a workflow should not convert an existing `FORCED_SUCCESS` state to `SUCCESS`.

### How to reproduce

1. Create a workflow containing at least two sequential tasks: `A -> B`.
2. Run the workflow and make task A fail.
3. Perform the "Force Success" operation on task A.
4. Confirm that the state of task A is `FORCED_SUCCESS`.
5. Perform the "Recovery Failed" operation on the workflow instance.
6. Wait for downstream task B to start.
7. Check the state of task A again.

Actual result:

```text
FORCED_SUCCESS -> SUCCESS
```

Expected result:

```text
FORCED_SUCCESS -> FORCED_SUCCESS
```

### Anything else

The issue is still present in the `dev` branch at commit:

```text
eca5d5e3df52f812c7820b5da6de5feb5cc140e4
```

The relevant source-code path is:

1. `RecoverFailureTaskCommandHandler` retains a `FORCED_SUCCESS` task instance when rebuilding the workflow execution graph because only `FAILURE`, `KILL`, and `PAUSE` tasks are recreated or recovered.
2. The retained task receives a `TaskStartLifecycleEvent` when the recovered workflow starts processing the execution graph.
3. `TaskForceSuccessStateAction` inherits the start-event behavior from `TaskSuccessStateAction`.
4. The inherited success handling unconditionally persists the task state as `TaskExecutionStatus.SUCCESS`.

Relevant files:

- `dolphinscheduler-master/.../command/handler/RecoverFailureTaskCommandHandler.java`
- `dolphinscheduler-master/.../task/statemachine/TaskForceSuccessStateAction.java`
- `dolphinscheduler-master/.../task/statemachine/TaskSuccessStateAction.java`
- `dolphinscheduler-master/.../task/statemachine/AbstractTaskStateAction.java`

This does not prevent downstream execution, but it removes the audit distinction between a normally successful task and a manually forced-success task.

### Version

dev

cases.issue_title: [Bug] [Dependent Task] Selecting ALL for a task dependency throws Invalid key format
cases.issue_body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I had searched in the [issues](https://github.com/apache/dolphinscheduler/issues?q=is%3Aissue) and found no similar issues.

### What happened

When a Dependent task is configured with **Dependent Type** set to **Dependent On Task** and **Task Name** set to `ALL`, the task fails while processing the dependency result:

```text
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Invalid key format
    at org.apache.dolphinscheduler.plugin.task.api.model.DependentItem.fromKey(DependentItem.java:48)
    at org.apache.dolphinscheduler.server.master.engine.executor.plugin.dependent.DependentTaskTracker.isAllDependentTaskFinished(DependentTaskTracker.java:245)
```

The generated task parameters contain `depTaskCode: -1`:

```json
{
  "dependentType": "DEPENDENT_ON_TASK",
  "projectCode": 1001,
  "definitionCode": 2001,
  "depTaskCode": -1,
  "cycle": "day",
  "dateValue": "today",
  "parameterPassing": false
}
```

In the official `dev` branch, the UI assigns `-1` to the `ALL` option:

```typescript
taskList.unshift({
  value: -1,
  label: 'ALL',
  filterLabel: 'ALL'
})
```

`DependentItem#getKey()` then produces a key similar to:

```text
2001--1-day-today
```

`DependentItem#fromKey()` splits the key using `key.split("-")` and requires exactly four parts. A negative task code introduces an additional hyphen, so the key is split into five parts and `Invalid key format` is thrown.

### What you expected to happen

When **Dependent Type** is **Dependent On Task** and **Task Name** is `ALL`, the Dependent task should check all tasks in the selected workflow and calculate the dependency result without throwing a key-format exception.

### How to reproduce

1. Create and run a workflow that will be used as the dependency target.
2. Add a Dependent task to another workflow.
3. Set **Dependent Type** to **Dependent On Task**.
4. Select the target project and workflow.
5. Set **Task Name** to `ALL`.
6. Set **Cycle** to `day` and the date option to `today`.
7. Run the workflow containing the Dependent task.
8. The Dependent task throws `Invalid key format` while processing the dependency result.

### Anything else

The official constant defines `-1` as the special code for all tasks:

```java
public static final long DEPENDENT_ALL_TASK_CODE = -1;
```

The same `fromKey()` implementation is currently present in both the official `dev` and `3.4.2-release` branches.

dev

cases.issue_title: [Bug] [API] Enforce permission checks for sub-workflow references
cases.issue_body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I had searched in the issues and found no similar issues.

### What happened

When a workflow or task definition contains a sub-workflow task, the API verifies the user's write permission for the parent project, but it does not consistently verify write permission for the project that owns the referenced workflow before the reference is persisted or activated. As a result, a user may bind a sub-workflow from a project that the user cannot modify.

### What you expected to happen

Before a sub-workflow reference is created, changed, or activated, the API should resolve the referenced workflow and verify that the user has write permission for its project. ### How to reproduce

1. Create projects A and B.
2. Grant a user write permission for project A, but not project B.
3. Create a workflow in project B.
4. As that user, create or update a workflow in project A with a sub-workflow task that references the workflow in project B.
5. Observe that the reference can be persisted without consistently checking write permission for project B.

### Anything else

The permission check should cover workflow creation and updates, workflow-instance updates, version switching, and online or release operations.

This issue is limited to permission enforcement when a sub-workflow reference is created, changed, or activated. It does not add pre-execution dependency validation for a sub-workflow that becomes unavailable after it was bound; that remains part of the existing runtime failure behavior.

cases.issue_title: [Bug] [Module Name] Overloaded master excludes itself from slot rebalance, permanently stops consuming commands (self-starvation deadlock)
cases.issue_body:
### Search before asking - [x] I had searched in the [issues](https://github.com/apache/dolphinscheduler/issues?q=is%3Aissue) and found no similar issues. ### What happened On a standalone deployment, the master can enter a state where it permanently stops consuming commands and never recovers without a restart. Commands pile up in t_ds_command while the master logs The current server is overload, cannot consumes commands. indefinitely. We traced it to a self-reinforcing loop between server-load protection and slot rebalancing: 1.A scheduling burst pushes the live workflow-instance count above master.server-load-protection.max-concurrent-workflow-instances. MasterServerLoadProtection.isOverload() returns true and the master reports itself as ServerStatus.BUSY in its heartbeat. 2.MasterSlotManager.doReBalance() looks for the current master inside the NORMAL-only server list: `// MasterClusters.getNormalServers() .filter(masterServer -> masterServer.getServerStatus() == ServerStatus.NORMAL)` Because the master just marked itself BUSY, it is no longer in that list, so it cannot find itself: `WARN MasterSlotManager - Do rebalance failed, cannot found the current master: 172.18.0.2:5678` currentSlot is set to -1. 3.IdSlotBasedCommandFetcher.fetchCommands() then short-circuits: `WARN IdSlotBasedCommandFetcher - MasterSlotManager check slot (-1 -> 1) is invalidated.` No commands are fetched at all. 4.Commands accumulate. Any workflow instance already created but stuck (see the secondary issue below) keeps the instance count above the threshold, so the master stays BUSY forever. The condition that stops the master from working is the same condition that prevents it from recovering. **Secondary issue: duplicate command handling leaks tasks** While the slot flaps between valid and invalid, an already-fetched-but-not-yet-deleted command can be fetched a second time. Deduplication relies on the delete succeeding: `// WorkflowExecutionFactory.deleteCommandOrThrow() boolean deleteResult = commandDao.deleteById(command.getId()); if (!deleteResult) { throw new CommandDuplicateHandleException(command); }` The second handler throws, and CommandEngine marks the workflow instance FAILURE and moves the command to t_ds_error_command. But the first handler has already published TaskStartLifecycleEvent and inserted the task into the task-group queue. The result is an inconsistent pair that nothing ever reconciles: - t_ds_workflow_instance.state = 6 (FAILURE) (or stuck at 1 RUNNING) - t_ds_task_instance.state = 0 (SUBMITTED), start_time/host/pid all null, no log file Those workflow instances count toward max-concurrent-workflow-instances forever, which feeds straight back into step 1. ### What you expected to happen 1.A master should not exclude itself from slot rebalancing because of its own load status. Load protection should throttle intake, not make the node invisible to its own slot computation — otherwise overload becomes unrecoverable. 2.When CommandDuplicateHandleException is raised, the tasks already dispatched by the winning handler should be reconciled rather than left in state=0 indefinitely. ### How to reproduce 1.Standalone deployment, single master. 2.Set master.server-load-protection.max-concurrent-workflow-instances below the size of one scheduling burst (we had ~44 workflows firing on the same cron tick with the limit at 20). 3.Let it run. Each burst trips overload; occasionally a duplicate-handled command leaves a workflow instance stuck. Once the number of stuck instances reaches the limit, the master stops consuming commands permanently. ### Anything else

Observed impact

cases.issue_title: [Bug] [Master] Task retry is delayed by the elapsed time instead of being scheduled at (endTime + retryInterval)
cases.issue_body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I had searched in the [issues](https://github.com/apache/dolphinscheduler/issues?q=is%3Aissue) and found no similar issues.


### What happened

When a task fails and still has retry attempts left, the master schedules a delayed
`TaskRetryLifecycleEvent`. The delay is computed in
`TaskRetryLifecycleEvent#of`:

```java
final long remainingTime =
        TimeUnit.MINUTES.toMillis(delayTime) + System.currentTimeMillis() - taskInstance.getEndTime().getTime();
```

The intent is "retry the task at `endTime + retryInterval`", so the remaining delay should be

```
retryInterval - (now - endTime)
```

but the expression actually evaluates to

```
retryInterval + (now - endTime)
```

The elapsed time since the task ended is **added** to the delay instead of being
**subtracted** from it. The signs of `now` and `endTime` are swapped.


### What you expected to happen

The retry should fire `retryInterval` after the task ended. If the retry interval has
already elapsed by the time the event is created, the task should be retried
immediately.

## Impact

In the common path (`onFailedEvent` fires milliseconds after the task ended) the error is
only a few milliseconds and is invisible.

It becomes significant whenever the retry event is created **long after** the task
actually ended, because the delay then grows without bound:

* **Master failover.** `WorkflowFailoverCommandHandler#assembleWorkflowExecutionGraph`
  rebuilds the execution graph from the *existing* task instances, so a task instance
  left in `FAILURE` with retries remaining is preserved as-is. When the workflow is
  re-triggered, `TaskFailureStateAction#onStartEvent` republishes a
  `TaskFailedLifecycleEvent` carrying the **stale** `endTime` read from the database.
  `TaskRetryLifecycleEvent#of` then computes `retryInterval + (now - endTime)`, so the
  retry is postponed by the whole outage duration on top of the configured interval.
  A task that failed an hour before the failover, with a 1-minute retry interval, waits
  ~61 minutes instead of being retried immediately.
* Any other path where the failure event is processed after a delay (event backlog,
  workflow paused/resumed) is skewed the same way.

The workflow simply looks stuck in `RUNNING_EXECUTION` while the retry sits in the delay
queue.


### How to reproduce

1. Define a workflow with one task that fails, with `failRetryTimes >= 1` and
   `failRetryInterval = 1` (minute).
2. Run it and let the task fail so it enters `FAILURE` while waiting to retry.
3. Kill the master that owns the workflow instance before the retry fires.
4. Wait a few minutes, then let another master pick the instance up by failover.
5. The retry is scheduled `1 minute + <outage duration>` in the future instead of firing
   right away.

A deterministic unit-level reproduction: call `TaskRetryLifecycleEvent.of(taskExecution)`
with a task instance whose `endTime` is two hours in the past and whose `retryInterval`
is 5 minutes. Expected delay: `0`. Actual delay: `~2h05m`.


### Anything else

The same expression is the only place the retry delay is computed, so the fix is
confined to `TaskRetryLifecycleEvent#of`.

### Version

cases.issue_title: [Bug] [Master] Recovered failed task keeps the exhausted retryTimes and never retries
cases.issue_body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I had searched in the [issues](https://github.com/apache/dolphinscheduler/issues?q=is%3Aissue) and found no similar issues.


### What happened

When a workflow is recovered with "Recover failed tasks"
(`CommandType.START_FAILURE_TASK_PROCESS`), `RecoverFailureTaskCommandHandler` recreates
every `FAILURE` / `KILL` task instance through `FailedRecoverTaskInstanceFactory`. That
factory clones the old task instance, clears part of its runtime state and inserts it as a
brand-new row, marking the old one `flag = NO`:

```java
final TaskInstance taskInstance = cloneTaskInstance(needRecoverTaskInstance);
taskInstance.setId(null);
taskInstance.setState(TaskExecutionStatus.SUBMITTED_SUCCESS);
taskInstance.setHost(null);
taskInstance.setVarPool(null);
taskInstance.setSubmitTime(new Date());
taskInstance.setLogPath(null);
taskInstance.setExecutePath(null);
taskInstanceDao.insert(taskInstance);
```

`AbstractTaskInstanceFactory#cloneTaskInstance` copies `retryTimes`, `startTime`,
`endTime`, `pid` and `alertFlag`, and the factory never resets them.

A task that failed after using up its retries has `retryTimes == maxRetryTimes`. The
recreated instance therefore starts life with a **fully consumed retry budget**, because
`TaskExecution#isTaskInstanceCanRetry()` is

```java
return taskInstance.getRetryTimes() < taskInstance.getMaxRetryTimes();
```

So on the recovery run the task fails permanently on its very first failure and is never
retried, even though the task definition asks for N retries.

The stale `startTime` / `endTime` are also carried over, so until the task actually starts
the new instance is displayed with the timestamps of the previous failed attempt, and
`TaskInstanceServiceImpl#queryTaskListPaging` computes its duration from them
(`DateUtils.format2Duration(startTime, endTime)`).


### What you expected to happen

The recreated task instance is a new attempt, so it should get the whole retry budget back
and should not inherit the runtime state of the failed attempt — exactly like the two
sibling factories do:

* `FirstRunTaskInstanceFactory` sets `retryTimes(0)`, `startTime(null)`, `endTime(null)`,
  `alertFlag(NO)`.
* `RetryTaskInstanceFactory` sets `startTime(null)`, `endTime(null)`, `pid(0)` and
  deliberately increments `retryTimes`.

`FailedRecoverTaskInstanceFactory` is the odd one out.


### How to reproduce

1. Create a workflow with one task that fails, and set **Failed retry times = 3**,
   **Failed retry interval = 1**.
2. Run it. The task retries 3 times, then the task and the workflow end in `FAILURE`.
   The last task instance has `retry_times = 3`, `max_retry_times = 3`.
3. On the workflow instance, click **Recover failed tasks**.
4. Expected: the task runs again and, if it keeps failing, retries up to 3 more times.
   Actual: the task runs once, fails, and is not retried at all — the workflow goes
   straight back to `FAILURE`.
5. Check `t_ds_task_instance`: the newly inserted row already has `retry_times = 3`, plus
   the `start_time` / `end_time` / `pid` of the previous failed attempt.


### Anything else

Every recovery of a retry-exhausted task is affected, so the workaround is to click
"Recover failed tasks" repeatedly, which is what the retry configuration was supposed to
do automatically.

This is the same class of bug as #16991 (`FailedRecoverTaskInstanceFactory` not setting
`environmentConfig`), in the same factory, but a different set of fields. #16991 was
resolved by resolving the environment centrally in `TaskExecutionContextFactory`, so the
two do not overlap.

cases.issue_title: MarkdownEditor: typing becomes O(document) with large content — auto-height defeats CodeMirror's viewport rendering
cases.issue_body:
> _Provenance: this report and its reproduction repository were generated by Claude (Anthropic's Claude Code) from a real problem in a production Filament app. Measurements are from automated browser probes; the repro was verified before filing. Flagging the AI authorship for transparency._

### Package

Forms

### Package Version

v5.7.1

### Laravel Version

v13.20.0

### Livewire Version

v4.3.3

### PHP Version

PHP 8.4.23

### Problem description

With a large document (~30kb of markdown, ~1,100 lines) in a `MarkdownEditor`, every keystroke costs ~40-60ms on a fast machine, making typing visibly laggy. Small documents are fine (~2.5ms/keystroke).

Measured decomposition (headless Chromium, real edit page): `editor.value()` costs 0.2ms and the Livewire-entangled state write 0.1ms per keystroke — but a keystroke with **all** `change`/`update` handlers detached still costs ~42ms. The cost is inside CodeMirror's display update.

Root cause: EasyMDE renders the editor at full content height (`.CodeMirror { height: auto }`) and `MarkdownEditor` sets no height cap, so CodeMirror 5's viewport rendering is defeated — every line of the document stays in the rendered DOM and each keystroke re-measures all of them. Confirmed by probe: constraining the scroller height drops rendered lines from ~1,100 to ~40 and keystroke cost from ~42ms to ~3.4ms (a ~14× improvement). `previewImagesInEditor: true` compounds it: `handleImages` runs on every `update` with a layout-forcing `innerText` read per rendered `.cm-image-marker`.

Note `->maxHeight()` is not an adequate default fix: it is forwarded to EasyMDE as a **fixed** `height`, so a 3-line editor then renders as a large empty box. A CSS `max-height` on `.fi-fo-markdown-editor .CodeMirror:not(.CodeMirror-fullscreen) .CodeMirror-scroll` keeps small editors compact while restoring viewport rendering for large ones — that is the workaround we shipped.

### Expected behavior

Typing latency in `MarkdownEditor` should stay roughly constant regardless of document length (O(viewport), not O(document)), as it does for a small document.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Clone the reproduction repo below, `composer install`, `cp .env.example .env`, `php artisan key:generate`, `touch database/database.sqlite`, `php artisan migrate --seed`, `php artisan serve`.
2. Log in at `/admin` (`admin@example.com` / `password`) and open **Markdown Editor Repro**; expand the **Markdown Content** section.
3. Type in the editor — each keystroke stutters. The README includes a console snippet that reports rendered line count and ms/keystroke (~1,100 lines, ~42ms), and shows both drop (~40 lines, ~3.4ms) the moment a `max-height` cap is applied.

### Reproduction repository (issue will be closed if this is not valid)

https://github.com/tonypiper/filament-markdown-editor-repro

### Relevant log output

_No response_

cases.issue_title: MarkdownEditor: inline image previews don't render until the first keystroke when the editor initializes hidden (collapsed Section / hidden Tab)
cases.issue_body:
> _Provenance: this report and its reproduction repository were generated by Claude (Anthropic's Claude Code) from a real problem in a production Filament app. Measurements are from automated browser probes; the repro was verified before filing. Flagging the AI authorship for transparency._

### Package

Forms

### Package Version

v5.7.1

### Laravel Version

v13.20.0

### Livewire Version

v4.3.3

### PHP Version

PHP 8.4.23

### Problem description

`MarkdownEditor` enables EasyMDE's `previewImagesInEditor`, but when the editor sits inside an initially-collapsed `Section` (or a non-active `Tab`), inline image previews don't render when the user expands the section — the raw `![...](...)` markdown stays visible until the user **types a character** (or otherwise forces a CodeMirror update). Verified in headless Chromium with a visible `data:` URI image: **zero** previews after expanding the section with no typing, deterministically across 5/5 runs; previews appear immediately after the first keystroke.

Root cause: EasyMDE applies previews from a CodeMirror `update` handler (`this.codemirror.on('update', handleImages)`). The editor initializes while its container is hidden, rendering zero lines, so the init-time update passes run with nothing to preview. Expanding the section fires **no** CodeMirror update, and with an auto-height editor no scroll event produces one either — so the first update after reveal is the user's first keystroke. A bare `cm.refresh()` once visible applies the previews immediately, isolating the bug to "no update pass runs on reveal".

Independent of the large-document typing-lag issue #20218: capping the editor height (the fix there) does **not** fix this — with the cap applied the editor renders a bounded ~40-line viewport but previews still stay raw until the first keystroke (0 previews before typing, 5/5 runs).

### Expected behavior

Inline image previews should render when the editor becomes visible (on section expand / tab activation), without requiring a keystroke.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Clone the reproduction repo below, `composer install`, `cp .env.example .env`, `php artisan key:generate`, `touch database/database.sqlite`, `php artisan migrate --seed`, `php artisan serve`.
2. Log in at `/admin` (`admin@example.com` / `password`) and open **Markdown Editor Repro**; expand the **Markdown Content** section.
3. Observe the images render as raw `![...](data:...)` markdown, not preview boxes (`document.querySelectorAll('[data-img-src]').length` is `0`).
4. Type any character — the previews appear.

Minimal form shape: `Section::make()->collapsed()->schema([MarkdownEditor::make('content')])` with content containing an image on its own line.

cases.issue_title: Tab badge icons throw a TypeError when using a BackedEnum
cases.issue_body:
### Package

filament/filament

### Package Version

5.7.1

### Laravel Version

13.21.0

### Livewire Version

v4.3.3

### PHP Version

8.4.22 

### Problem description

Using a `BackedEnum`, such as a `Heroicon`, with `Tabs\Tab::badgeIcon()` causes a `TypeError` when the tabs are rendered.

  The public `Tab::badgeIcon()` method accepts `BackedEnum`, and `Tab::getBadgeIcon()` may also return a `BackedEnum`. However,
  `Tabs::generateTabBadgeHtml()` only accepts `string|Htmlable|null` for its `$icon` argument.

  As a result, the following valid configuration fails during rendering:

  ```php
  Tab::make('Products')
      ->badge('Available')
      ->badgeIcon(Heroicon::OutlinedCheckCircle)

  The exception is:

  Filament\Schemas\Components\Tabs::generateTabBadgeHtml():
  Argument #3 ($icon) must be of type
  Illuminate\Contracts\Support\Htmlable|string|null,
  Filament\Support\Icons\Heroicon given

  This appears to be a regression introduced in Filament 5.7.0 when tab badge rendering was extracted into generateTabBadgeHtml().

  In earlier versions, the badge icon was passed directly to generate_icon_html(), which already accepts string|BackedEnum|Htmlable|
  null.


### Expected behavior

```markdown
  A tab badge icon configured with a `BackedEnum`, including a `Heroicon`, should render without throwing an exception.

  The internal renderer should support the same icon types accepted by the public `Tab::badgeIcon()` API.

  For example, this should render successfully:

  ```php
  Tab::make('Products')
      ->badge('Available')
      ->badgeIcon(Heroicon::OutlinedCheckCircle)




### Steps to reproduce

  ```markdown
  1. Create a fresh Laravel application with Filament 5.7.1.
  2. Create a Filament page or resource containing a schema with tabs.
  3. Add a badge and a Heroicon badge icon to one of the tabs:

  ```php
  use Filament\Schemas\Components\Tabs;
  use Filament\Schemas\Components\Tabs\Tab;
  use Filament\Support\Icons\Heroicon;

  Tabs::make('Status')
      ->tabs([
          Tab::make('Products')
              ->badge('Available')
              ->badgeIcon(Heroicon::OutlinedCheckCircle)
              ->schema([]),
      ])

  4. Open the page containing the tabs.
  5. A TypeError is thrown by Tabs::generateTabBadgeHtml().

  Changing the icon to its string value avoids the exception:

  ->badgeIcon(Heroicon::OutlinedCheckCircle->value)

  However, this workaround should not be necessary because badgeIcon() explicitly accepts BackedEnum.

cases.issue_title: Modal close scroll-jumps to the restored-focus element on body-scroll layouts (regression in v5.7.0)
cases.issue_body:
### Package

filament/filament

### Package Version

v5.7.1 (regression introduced in v5.7.0; last good: v5.6.8)

### Laravel Version

v13.20.0

### Livewire Version

v4.3.3

### PHP Version

8.4.23

### Problem description

Since v5.7.0, closing any modal (confirmation/action modal, delete confirmation, etc.) scroll-jumps the page. When the page is scrolled down and the document (`<html>`/`body`) is the scroll container, closing the modal scrolls the page up to the element that had focus before the modal opened — typically the main content wrapper (`main.fi-main`, which carries `tabindex="-1"`). The page visibly "jerks."

**Cause:** the modal component's focus trap lost the `.noscroll` modifier in v5.7.0.

`packages/support/resources/views/components/modal/index.blade.php`

```diff
- x-trap.noscroll{{ $focusTrapReturnsFocus ? '' : '.noreturn' }}{{ $autofocus ? '' : '.noautofocus' }}="isTrapActive"
+ x-trap{{ $focusTrapReturnsFocus ? '' : '.noreturn' }}{{ $autofocus ? '' : '.noautofocus' }}="isTrapActive"
```

When the trap deactivates on close, Alpine returns focus to the previously-focused element via `.focus()`, which scrolls that element into view. `.noscroll` previously suppressed this. Without it, the browser scrolls the document to the restored-focus target.

It appears `.noscroll` was dropped as part of moving scroll-locking into Filament's own JS (likely to resolve the nested-modal stuck-scroll-lock issue, #10925 / alpinejs/alpine#3435), but that also removed the scroll suppression around focus restoration.

**Browser note:** it's browser/layout dependent. Chrome uses `block: "nearest"` semantics for focus scrolling, so it does NOT scroll when the restored-focus element already fills the viewport (tall content / large viewport). It reproduces reliably when the restored-focus target is shorter than the viewport (short-content pages) or in browsers that scroll on focus regardless.

### Expected behavior

Closing a modal should not scroll the page. Focus can still be returned to the previously-focused element (accessibility), but without scrolling to it — as `x-trap.noscroll` did prior to v5.7.0.

### Steps to reproduce

1. A panel page tall enough that the document scrolls (the whole page/body is the scroll container).
2. Scroll down so a modal trigger (e.g. a table header action with `->requiresConfirmation()`) is near the top of the viewport but the main content wrapper's top is above the fold.
3. Click the trigger to open the confirmation modal.
4. Click Confirm (or Cancel / press Escape).
5. Observe the page scroll-jump upward as the modal closes.

Most reliable on a short-content page (so `main.fi-main` is shorter than the viewport) and in a browser that scrolls on programmatic focus.

### Reproduction repository (issue will be closed if this is not valid)

https://github.com/the14thsky/filament-demo

cases.issue_title: SpatieMediaLibraryFileUpload reorder callback discards saved state, leaving a consumed TemporaryUploadedFile in the form state
cases.issue_body:
### Package

filament/spatie-laravel-media-library-plugin

### Package Version

v5.7.1

### Laravel Version

v13.20.0

### Livewire Version

v4.3.3

### PHP Version

PHP 8.4.16

### Problem description

Adding a file to a `SpatieMediaLibraryFileUpload` that lives inside a `Repeater` bound to an **already persisted** record throws:

```
League\Flysystem\UnableToRetrieveMetadata
Unable to retrieve the file_size for file at location: livewire-tmp/<hash>.pdf
```

`BaseFileUpload::saveUploadedFiles()` stores the media, deletes the Livewire temporary file, and hands the resulting state to the reorder callback under the injection name `state`:

```php
// packages/forms/src/Components/BaseFileUpload.php
if ($this->isReorderable && ($callback = $this->reorderUploadedFilesUsing)) {
    $rawState = $this->evaluate($callback, [
        'state' => $rawState,
    ]);
}
```

The callback registered by the plugin declares that parameter as `$rawState`:

```php
// packages/spatie-laravel-media-library-plugin/src/Forms/Components/SpatieMediaLibraryFileUpload.php
$this->reorderUploadedFilesUsing(static function (SpatieMediaLibraryFileUpload $component, ?Model $record, array $rawState): array {
    // ...
    return $rawState;
});
```

`rawState` is not among the named injections, so `EvaluatesClosures::resolveClosureDependencyForEvaluation()` falls through to `Component::resolveDefaultClosureDependencyForEvaluationByName('rawState')`, which returns `$this->getRawState()` — the **pre-save** Livewire state. The callback returns that, overwriting the state `saveUploadedFiles()` had just built.

Logging the callback's input and output shows it directly:

```
in:  {"<existing-uuid>": "<existing-uuid>", "newfilekey": "<uuid-of-stored-media>"}
out: {"<existing-uuid>": "<existing-uuid>", "newfilekey": TemporaryUploadedFile}
```

So the media is stored correctly, but a `TemporaryUploadedFile` whose backing file has just been deleted stays in the form state.

That is normally invisible, because the state is reloaded from the relationship right after saving. It becomes fatal inside a `Repeater`, because `Schema::saveRelationships()` saves child schemas *before* the component itself:

```php
// packages/schemas/src/Concerns/BelongsToModel.php
foreach ($component->getChildSchemas(...) as $childSchema) {
    $childSchema->saveRelationships();   // upload runs here, temp file deleted
}

$component->saveRelationships();         // repeater runs here
```

and `Repeater::saveToRelationship()` then re-validates every item against that stale state:

```php
// packages/forms/src/Components/Repeater.php
foreach ($this->getItems() as $itemKey => $item) {
    $itemData = $item->getState(shouldCallHooksBefore: false); // validates again
```

On that second pass the `maxSize()` rule calls `getSize()` on the deleted temp file and Flysystem throws.

Only **existing** records are affected. For new repeater items `Component::saveRelationships()` returns early at `if (! ($this->getRecord()?->exists))`, and the upload runs after validation via `$item->model($record)->saveRelationships()`.

Both `->reorderable()` and `->maxSize()` are needed to surface the exception: `reorderable()` is what makes `saveUploadedFiles()` call the reorder callback at all, and `maxSize()` adds the `max:` rule that reads the file size. Dropping either one hides the exception, but the stale state is still written in both cases.

The same parameter mismatch is present on the `5.x` and `4.x` branches.

### Expected behavior

The reorder callback should receive and return the state that `saveUploadedFiles()` passed it, so the stored media UUID survives and no consumed `TemporaryUploadedFile` is left behind in the form state.

Renaming the closure parameter in `SpatieMediaLibraryFileUpload::setUp()` from `$rawState` to `$state` is enough — `evaluate()` then resolves it from the explicit injection:

```diff
-$this->reorderUploadedFilesUsing(static function (SpatieMediaLibraryFileUpload $component, ?Model $record, array $rawState): array {
+$this->reorderUploadedFilesUsing(static function (SpatieMediaLibraryFileUpload $component, ?Model $record, array $state): array {
```

(and the corresponding `$rawState` references in the body). Applying that to `vendor/` makes the test in the reproduction repository pass.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `Contract` hasMany `Addendum`; `Addendum` implements `HasMedia`.
2. On the Contract edit form, a `Repeater` bound to `addendums` containing:

```php
SpatieMediaLibraryFileUpload::make('attachment')
    ->collection(Addendum::ADDENDUM_MEDIA)
    ->multiple()
    ->reorderable()
    ->maxSize(10000),
```

3. Make sure an addendum already exists as a persisted record and already has a file.
4. Reopen the contract, add a second file to that existing addendum, and save.

In the reproduction repository this is all seeded already:

```bash
composer install
cp .env.example .env
php artisan key:generate
touch database/database.sqlite
php artisan migrate:fresh --seed
php artisan test
```

The test fails with the exception above. For the browser: `php artisan serve`, log in at `/admin` with `test@example.com` / `password`, open **Contracts → Contract A → Edit**, add a file to the existing addendum and save.

One thing worth flagging: `TemporaryUploadedFile::getSize()` has an `if (app()->runningUnitTests())` branch that reads metadata instead of touching the disk, so under PHPUnit the missing file normally goes unnoticed. The test sets `$this->app['env'] = 'local'` so the validator really stats the file, exactly as it does in a real request. That line only removes the mask — it does not create the bug.

### Reproduction repository (issue will be closed if this is not valid)

https://github.com/RobbeReygel/filament-issue-repro

### Relevant log output

```shell
League\Flysystem\UnableToRetrieveMetadata: Unable to retrieve the file_size for file at location: livewire-tmp/EJlL6ZYGe5LLHKk62iNtIIfs2rs9n3Hztgr6lWiY.pdf.

### Issue Summary

Issue Summary
When a members CSV import has failed rows, the error file downloaded from the Admin import modal is built client-side from the raw API rows. Array fields like labels are serialized as [object Object], and the columns use internal field names (subscribed) instead of the export headers (subscribed_to_emails).

This makes the downloaded report unusable for the fix-and-re-upload workflow: re-importing it creates a label literally named [object Object] on the member (labels are created on import), and the subscribed column is ignored because that header isn't in the import mapping. The emailed error report formats these fields correctly, so the two reports disagree.

Where it happens: apps/admin/src/members/components/bulk-action-modals/import-members/csv.ts passes the raw rows to Papa.unparse, while the server-side emailed report (completion-email.ts) maps rows to the export vocabulary first. Happy to open a PR that makes the download match the emailed report.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. In Admin, import a members CSV where at least one row fails (e.g. an invalid email) and that row has labels.
2. Download the error file from the import modal.
3. Open it: the labels column contains [object Object] and the header row uses subscribed rather than subscribed_to_emails.
4. Fix the reported error in the file and re-upload it: the member is created with an [object Object] label and the subscription state from the file is dropped.

cases.issue_body:
### Issue Summary

The migration `2026-08-11-21-22-48-rename-email-batches-provider-id.js` uses index mode `{algorithm: 'instant'}`.  This was introduced in MySQL 8.0.28 (https://dev.mysql.com/doc/relnotes/mysql/8.0/en/news-8-0-28.html#mysqld-8-0-28-feature), causing prior versions to fail the migration.

I ran into this as I use a hosted MySQL database with little possibility for manually upgrading.

The Ghost documentation does not say MySQL 8.0.28 or newer is required, only requiring MySQL 8.0 or 8.4 (https://docs.ghost.org/hosting).  Same on several other pages.

The issue can be worked around by manually replacing the index creation mode to `{algorithm: 'inplace'}` or `{algorithm: 'auto'}` (like all other migrations seem to use), clearing the `knex` lock and re-running the migration.

Ghost should either clarify the exact required version of MySQL or refrain from using index mode instant as long as MySQL 8.0 is supported.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Ghost 6.0.57 on MySQL 8.0.27 or earlier (I used 8.0.21)
2. Upgrade to Ghost 6.0.58

cases.issue_title: `card_assets` exclude no longer excludes the header card since the prebuilt manifest refactor
cases.issue_body:
## Issue Summary

Since #29659 (`cbe73b18a`, "Fixed card assets busting caches on every Ghost restart"), a theme declaring `"card_assets": {"exclude": ["header"]}` still receives header card CSS in `/public/cards.min.css`, overriding the theme's own `.kg-header-card` styles.

The header card ships two source files, `core/frontend/src/cards/css/header.css` and `core/frontend/src/cards/css/header_v2.css`, but only one documented card name, `header`. Before the refactor, exclusion was done with a `tiny-glob` pattern and both files were dropped. Now it is an exact string comparison against the manifest keys, so `header_v2` survives.

Old:

```js
return {
    'cards.min.css': `css/!(${this.config.exclude.join('|')}).css`,
    'cards.min.js': `js/!(${this.config.exclude.join('|')}).js`
};
```

New (`core/frontend/services/assets-minification/card-assets.js`, `getCardNames`):

```js
return available.filter(name => !this.config.exclude.includes(name));
```

The old behaviour was not really intentional. `tiny-glob` compiles extglob negation through `globrex` into a start-anchored negative lookahead rather than a full-string negation:

```js
globrex('!(header).css', {extended: true}).regex
// => /^(?!header)([^/]*)\.css$/
```

So `!(header).css` excluded `header.css` and, by prefix match, `header_v2.css` as well. Verified against the current card file names:

```
css/!(header).css  =>  audio, blockquote, bookmark, button, callout, collection,
                       cta, file, gallery, nft, product, signup, toggle,
                       transistor, video
```

`header` is the only card name in the manifest that is a strict prefix of another file name, so this is the only card affected. The `include` branch is unaffected, since `@(header).css` was already an exact match and never picked up `header_v2`.

Net effect: there is currently no documented way to exclude the header card's assets. `header_v2` works, but it is not in the [[card list in the theme docs](https://docs.ghost.org/themes/content)](https://docs.ghost.org/themes/content).

Two possible fixes:

1. Collapse `header_v2` into the `header` manifest key at build time in `scripts/build-card-assets.mjs`, so one documented name maps to all of that card's assets. This restores the previous behaviour for existing themes without touching the docs.
2. Keep the keys one-to-one and document `header_v2` (and the other undocumented keys, `collection`, `cta`, `transistor`) as excludable card names.

Option 1 seems preferable, since option 2 silently breaks every theme already shipping `"exclude": ["header"]` until each one is updated.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a theme whose `package.json` contains:
   ```json
   "config": {
       "card_assets": {
           "exclude": ["header"]
       }
   }
   ```
2. Activate the theme and restart Ghost.
3. Request `/public/cards.min.css`.

Expected: no `.kg-header-card` rules in the bundle, as was the case before #29659.

Actual: the contents of `header_v2.css` are present, and its `.kg-header-card` rules override the theme's own header card styles.

cases.issue_title: Process crash in 6.57.0 when got 13 accesses a cleared request after a redirect
cases.issue_body:
## Summary

A self-hosted Ghost `6.57.0` process exited with code `1` during publication of a post configured to send as a newsletter. The instance was supervised and restarted, but the campaign was left only partially materialized.

The sanitized crash signature was a `TypeError` involving access to `request.destroyed` in `got` request-stream code. The complete original stack was not retained, so I do not want to overstate the exact triggering endpoint.

## Installed runtime

- Ghost: `6.57.0`
- Node.js: `v22.23.2`
- Direct Ghost dependency at runtime: `got 13.0.0`

In the installed `got` source:

```js
// got/dist/source/core/index.js
// line 644
this._request = undefined;

// line 1022
if (!error && !this._request.destroyed) {
```

This looks vulnerable to a stale write callback observing a request after the redirect path has cleared/replaced `this._request`.

## Observed impact

- The process exit overlapped the `post.published` / newsletter-submission window.
- The application restarted automatically a few seconds later.
- A newsletter audience of 8,641 had started materializing; 2 batches reached the provider and 2,000 recipients were materialized before work stopped.
- At the first reconciliation, 1,978 deliveries and 18 recipient failures had been recorded, while 6,641 intended recipients had not been materialized.
- The mail provider/proxy remained healthy. The bulk provider path uses a different HTTP client, so this report does **not** attribute the crash to SES or the mail proxy.

The operational consequence is significant: a normal campaign retry could duplicate messages for recipients already accepted by the provider, so recovery has to be treated as a separate deduplication incident.

## Trigger confidence and limits

The publication has external `post.published` listeners. The failure mechanism is consistent with an outbound body request that receives a redirect while a previous write callback is still outstanding.

However:

- I have **not** identified a specific webhook/integration target as the trigger.
- I have **not** established that every redirect reproduces this behavior.
- A localhost test using ordinary `302` and `307` redirects did not reproduce the race deterministically.

The claim here is therefore limited to: the installed vulnerable code and the production crash signature match a known class of `got` redirect/stale-request races.

## Related `got` reports/fixes

These upstream reports appear closely related:

- https://github.com/sindresorhus/got/issues/2390
- https://github.com/sindresorhus/got/pull/2391
- https://github.com/sindresorhus/got/issues/2403
- https://github.com/sindresorhus/got/pull/2404
- https://github.com/sindresorhus/got/pull/2437

They cover crashes from accessing a request that no longer exists and subsequent guards for stale callbacks around redirects. `got 13.0.0` predates those fixes.

## Expected behavior

A failed or redirecting outbound publication listener should be reported as an ordinary request/listener failure. It should not be able to terminate the Ghost process or interrupt bulk newsletter materialization.

## Suggested next steps

1. Evaluate a compatible `got` update or a narrow backport of the upstream stale-callback guard.
2. Add a regression test that forces a redirect while an outbound POST/body write callback is still outstanding.
3. Ensure errors in outbound post-publication listeners cannot escape as a process-terminating exception.

I can provide additional sanitized timing/counter information if useful, but cannot share target URLs, recipient data, credentials, or raw request/response logs.

cases.issue_title: Autosave silently discards feature image alt text over 191 characters and prevents leaving editor view
cases.issue_body:
### Issue Summary

Feature image alt text longer than 191 characters silently fails to save, with no error shown anywhere in the UI, and the typed text is then discarded.

The editor autosaves on every keystroke, and autosave calls `saveTask` with `silent: true`. The catch block that surfaces validation errors is gated on `if (!options.silent)`, so the failure is dropped. The client-side validator invalidates the model before any request is made, so no HTTP request is ever sent: there is nothing in the network tab either.

An explicit save (Cmd+S) does show "Saving failed: Feature image alt text cannot be longer than 191 characters." So this only affects users relying on autosave, which is the default way the editor works.

Expected behaviour: the user should be told the alt text is too long, either by a validation message on the field, a `maxlength` on the input that prevents typing past the limit, or by surfacing validation errors even from silent saves. Currently the only clue is the "Are you sure you want to leave this page?" modal on navigating away, which does not say what is unsaved or why.

Worse, in one of two test runs the editor navigated away with no modal and no toast at all, silently discarding the alt text. The post status indicator can read "Draft - Saved" while an over-length value sits unsaved in the field.

Scope: this affects `feature_image_alt` on posts and pages only. Alt text on inline image cards, gallery cards and product cards is stored in the lexical document, has no length validation, and saves fine (confirmed at 5000 characters). This matters because writing genuinely descriptive alt text for a complex image routinely exceeds 191 characters, and accessibility guidance encourages it.

The limit counts Unicode code points, not bytes: 191 emoji (764 bytes) is accepted, while 192 plain ASCII characters is not.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a new draft post and set a feature image.
2. Click the "Alt" toggle under the feature image.
3. Type exactly 191 characters into the alt field and press Cmd+S. It saves, and a "Post saved" notification appears. This is the control.
4. Type one more character, so the field holds 192.
5. Wait for autosave and do not press Cmd+S. Observe: no error notification, no network request in devtools, and the post status changes to "Draft".
6. Navigate away using the "Posts" back arrow. Either the "you haven't saved all of your content" modal appears with no indication of what is wrong, or the editor navigates away with no warning at all.
7. Reopen the post. The alt text you typed is gone and an earlier, shorter value is in place.

For contrast, repeat with a 250-character alt text on an inline image card. It saves without complaint.

To see the server-side error that the editor never triggers, PUT over 191 characters to `/ghost/api/admin/posts/<id>/` directly.

### Ghost Version

6.38.0 (reproduced). Also reported on 6.53. The same validator and the same `silent: true` autosave are present in 5.130.6, so this is long-standing rather than a recent regression.

### Node.js Version

v22.22.2

### How did you install Ghost?

Official `ghost:6` Docker image, local development instance.

### Database type

SQLite3

### Browser & OS version

Official `ghost:6` Docker image, local development instance.

cases.issue_title: Member receives duplicate reply notification emails when authoring both the parent and in_reply_to comments
cases.issue_body:
### Issue Summary

When a reply is posted in a comment thread, Ghost notifies both the author of the thread's top-level comment (`parent_id`) and the author of the comment being replied to (`in_reply_to_id`). There is no deduplication between the two — when the same member authored both, they receive two identical emails for a single reply.

In `ghost/core/core/server/services/comments/comments-service.js`, `sendNewCommentNotifications`:
```
    if (comment.get('parent_id')) {
        await this.emails.notifyParentCommentAuthor(comment, {type: 'parent'});
    }
    if (comment.get('in_reply_to_id')) {
        await this.emails.notifyParentCommentAuthor(comment, {type: 'in_reply_to'});
    }
```
`notifyParentCommentAuthor` suppresses self-notification, but nothing compares the two recipients against each other — so both fire on every reply-to-a-reply, landing twice on the same member whenever they authored both comments.

This repeats every round of a back-and-forth thread: on our site, one 3-day exchange between two members produced ~18 doubled notifications to the thread starter, reported by the member as "I receive two emails every time someone replies to my comments."

Reproduced locally on a clean 6.53.0 install: a single reply produced two emails to the same member, same timestamp, distinct Message-IDs.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Member A posts a top-level comment (C1)
